items.stem: Which approach best achieves high availability for a stateless web tier in OCI?

options.text: Distribute instances across multiple availability/fault domains behind a load balancer
options.rationale: Correct: spreading instances and load-balancing removes single points of failure.
A single instance is a single point of failure.

options.text: Store everything on one block volume
options.rationale: One volume is a single point of failure, not HA.
Health checks are needed to route around failures.

items.stem: What must be true of CIDR blocks when peering two VCNs?

options.rationale: Correct: peered VCNs require non-overlapping CIDR ranges for routing to work.
Identical ranges overlap and cannot be routed.
Peering works with private ranges; public is not required.

options.text: They must be in the same subnet
options.rationale: Peered VCNs are separate networks, not one subnet.

items.stem: Which TWO improve disaster recovery for a critical OCI database?

options.rationale: Correct: a standby in another region protects against regional failure.

options.text: Defined and tested RTO/RPO with automated failover
options.rationale: Correct: documented, tested recovery objectives make DR reliable.

options.text: Keeping only a single backup in the same AD
options.rationale: A single co-located backup does not protect against AD/region loss.
Monitoring is needed to detect failures.
